title: Metering: add quantization_profile + runtime_config tags; propagate through ingestion to analytics
author: Nadia Rahman
description:
Context: Unit economics dashboard needs consistent drilldowns by quantization profile (fp16/int8/awq/etc) and by runtime execution config (batching/caching/kv settings bundle). Today metering events don’t carry these tags end-to-end, so the unit-econ pipeline can’t attribute cost deltas to profile adoption vs routing/mix shifts.

This PR adds two optional tags to metering events and wires them through ingestion to the curated analytics tables used by the unit-econ semantic layer.

What’s in this PR: (1) Metering event schema: add `quantization_profile` (string) and `runtime_config` (string) to the metering event payload; both are optional and default to null/"unknown" when absent. We do not include raw per-request config blobs; runtime_config is a stable, low-cardinality identifier (e.g. "rtcfg_v3_contbatch_kvcache_on") that is managed via a mapping table owned by Telemetry/Analytics. (2) Ingestion: propagate the new fields through metering ingestion (gateway -> ingestion service -> warehouse landing table), including validation/sanitization and reserved-value handling. (3) Warehouse + semantic layer: add columns to `analytics.metering_events_v2` and surface them in `analytics.unit_econ_request_facts` and daily rollup models (no change to existing rollup keys yet; these are additive dimensions intended for opt-in slicing). (4) Guardrails: cap cardinality on `runtime_config` via allowlist; unknown/unapproved values are coerced to "runtime_config_unmapped" and logged as a counter metric to avoid blowing up downstream group-bys. `quantization_profile` is validated against known profile names; unknown values become "unknown".

Schema details (illustrative): landing table `metering_events_raw` new columns: quantization_profile STRING NULLABLE; runtime_config STRING NULLABLE; plus a derived normalized version used in facts: quantization_profile_norm STRING NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'; runtime_config_norm STRING NOT NULL DEFAULT 'runtime_config_unmapped'.

Backfill/rollout: This is forward-compatible. Old events will have nulls in raw and "unknown"/"runtime_config_unmapped" in normalized columns. ENG-2918 will backfill 90 days once we confirm adoption from runtimes; this PR only adds the plumbing.

Tests: Added unit tests for payload parsing + normalization; integration test updates for the ingestion-to-warehouse contract; dbt model tests updated to assert the new columns exist and are non-null after normalization.

Operational notes: Added a counter metric `metering.tags.runtime_config.unmapped` and a weekly log sample (1/10k) to help us find new runtime_config values during rollouts without increasing telemetry volume materially.

Follow-ups: (a) wire runtime to emit the tags consistently across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (tracked in Applied ML + Runtime workstreams), (b) decide whether we expose these as first-class filters in the unit-econ dashboard MVP or keep behind an advanced toggle (cardinality risk), (c) add a dim table (`dim_runtime_config`) and documentation in the dataset dictionary once the set of configs stabilizes.

Risk assessment: low. Additive columns, no change to billing totals. Cardinality is explicitly bounded; reconciliation job should remain unchanged.
commits: metering: extend MeteringEvent schema with quantization_profile + runtime_config
ingestion: normalize/validate new metering tags; add unmapped counters
warehouse: add columns to metering_events_v2 landing + facts
dbt: surface tags in unit_econ_request_facts; update schema tests
docs/tests: update contract fixtures and golden files
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we guarantee runtime_config stays low-cardinality? We can’t afford surprises in the unit-econ group-bys.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yep — runtime_config is allowlisted in ingestion. Anything else becomes runtime_config_unmapped and increments a counter. We’ll only expand the allowlist via PR once we’re comfortable with the new value.
Thomas Baird (review): +1 on allowlist. Also: can we avoid storing raw config JSON anywhere? Even in logs?
Nadia Rahman (author): Agreed. This PR never logs raw blobs. The sample log is only the unmapped string value (post-sanitization) plus request_id hash prefix; no payload dump.
Cole Summers (review): Confirming: this doesn’t affect billing totals / invoice tie-out, right?
Nadia Rahman (author): Correct. Billing uses token counts + SKU pricing from metering; these are additive tags for analytics only. No changes to aggregation logic or pricing tables.
Arjun Desai (review): For quantization_profile values: can we standardize names now (e.g., awq_int4 vs int4_awq)?

Nadia Rahman (author): I added validation + normalization with a small mapping (awq_int4/int4_awq -> awq_int4). If the runtime emits something else, it lands as 'unknown' until we expand the map. We should align in the quant profile doc.
Logan Wright (review): Looks good. Please add a brief note in the dbt column docs about 'runtime_config_unmapped'.
Nadia Rahman (author): Done in schema.yml + model docs.
Arjun Desai (review): Approved after the normalization change.
release_notes: Internal-only: metering events now carry optional quantization_profile and runtime_config tags in analytics tables to enable unit economics attribution by profile/config. No customer-facing behavior changes.
